figure: FIGURE 11.1 — Discrete vs continuous batching (Orca-style slot diagram)
issue: The arrow from the annotation 'a finishing sequence frees its slot immediately' has its head landing within a few points of the green admission tick in the first continuous-panel row, so the reader cannot tell whether the annotation refers to the end of the preceding blue block (the finish) or to the green tick (the admission). The two readings are semantically different and the figure's whole argument turns on the distinction between 'slot freed' and 'slot backfilled'.
evidence: Rendered page: the arrow descends from the annotation text to the right-hand end of the first continuous-panel row, immediately adjacent to the narrow green band that the legend defines as 'admission event (backfill)'. The green band is only ~5 pt wide, so the arrowhead and the band are visually confusable at print size.
acceptance_test: Move the arrowhead so it clearly touches the right edge of the blue block with visible clearance from the green band, and/or add a distinct 'finish' marker (e.g. a small vertical tick at the sequence's end) so the two events are separately locatable. Acceptance: at 100% print size the arrowhead is unambiguously attached to one of the two events.

figure: FIGURE 11.1 — Discrete vs continuous batching (Orca-style slot diagram)
issue: The smallest in-figure annotations appear to sit at or below the 8 pt floor for figure text: the three-line green note ('a freed slot is backfilled at the green admission tick; the new sequence runs each batch's work block time (decode steps / iterations)') and the legend row. The green note is also the figure's only statement of the backfill rule, so it is load-bearing text that must be legible.
evidence: Rendered at 150 dpi, the green note's three lines occupy roughly 11-12 px line pitch (~6.5-7 pt type) and the legend row is comparable; the note also sits close to the 'time -> decode steps / iterations ->' axis label, so the two small-text elements are adjacent and compete.
acceptance_test: Measure the rendered cap-height of the legend row and the green note at 100% on the printed page (or extract their font sizes from the source) and confirm >= 8 pt; if under, enlarge the note and/or move the axis label to reduce competition. Acceptance: all figure annotation text measures >= 8 pt.

figure: FIGURE 11.4 — Three accelerator paths and one qualification gate
issue: The caption's parenthetical mis-maps the figure's contents. It reads '...through backend entry, kernels/runtime, and hardware Intel (torch.xpu or engine-native SYCL), Gaudi (hpu and its own stack), and client NPU (...)', which attaches 'torch.xpu or engine-native SYCL' to 'hardware'. In the figure, 'torch.xpu or engine-native SYCL' is the Backend entry cell of the Intel GPU column, and the Hardware cell reads 'Discrete GPU or integrated GPU'. The run-on also makes the three-column mapping hard to parse.
evidence: Rendered figure, Intel GPU column: Serving stack = 'vLLM XPU / SGLang XPU or llama.cpp SYCL'; Backend entry = 'torch.xpu or engine-native SYCL'; Kernels / runtime = 'GPU kernels / libraries / SYCL + Level Zero / matching GPU driver'; Hardware = 'Discrete GPU or integrated GPU'. The caption's parenthetical attaches the Backend-entry text to the Hardware level.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption as three explicit clauses, e.g. 'Intel GPU (backend entry: torch.xpu or engine-native SYCL), Gaudi (backend entry: PyTorch hpu and its own stack), and client NPU (backend entry: the OpenVINO NPU plugin; ...)'. Acceptance: every parenthetical in the caption maps to a named cell in the figure at the correct level.

figure: FIGURE 11.4 — Three accelerator paths and one qualification gate
issue: The smallest figure text — the three lines inside the qualification-gate box ('Weights + KV + workspace | operators + attention/cache path', 'Correctness + isolation | collectives (if used) | measured SLO', 'A visible device or a loaded model does not pass this gate.') and the trailing line 'Conceptual dependency map. Not cross-device API or feature equivalence implied.' — appears to render at or below the 8 pt floor. These lines carry the gate's actual criteria, which is the figure's payload.
evidence: Rendered at 150 dpi, the gate-box lines occupy roughly 12-13 px line pitch (~7 pt type) inside a box whose height is set by four stacked cells; the trailing italic line is smaller still.
acceptance_test: Measure the rendered size of the gate-box lines and the trailing italic line at 100% print size (or read their font sizes from the source) and confirm >= 8 pt; enlarge the gate box or reduce the figure's vertical whitespace if not. Acceptance: the gate criteria are legible at arm's length on a printed page.

figure: FIGURE 11.2 — Serving is four separate concerns, not a stack
issue: The figure asserts independence while its own note asserts an ordering, and the caption asserts interaction that the drawing does not show. The title says 'not a stack' and the caption says 'each is addressed in any order', but the in-figure note says 'Dashed border: a deployment-level concern, chosen after the engine internals (1-3)', which is a sequencing claim; and the caption's parenthetical '(they interact — batching pressure feeds KV residency — ...)' has no visual counterpart, since the four boxes are drawn as fully disconnected. A reader who takes the figure at face value will conclude the concerns are independent, which is the opposite of the caption's caveat.
evidence: Rendered page: four isolated boxes in a 2x2 grid with no arrows, no shared boundary, and no interaction annotation; the only relational statement is the note under the grid. The caption supplies the interaction verbally and even gives the concrete coupling (cached prefixes and live-batch pages drawing on the same 640 GB KV pool).
acceptance_test: Either add a minimal visual cue for the one coupling the caption names (e.g. a small dashed arrow from 1 REQUEST SCHEDULING to 2 STATE MANAGEMENT annotated 'batching pressure -> KV residency'), or reword the note to 'Dashed border: a deployment-level concern, configured after the engine internals (1-3) are chosen' and add 'the four interact; see caption' to the figure. Acceptance: the figure cannot be read as claiming the four concerns are independent.

issue: The in-plot formula f(r)=(S+P)/r contradicts the curve actually drawn in panel (a), and the caption repeats the wrong formula. The same note also contains two mutually inconsistent statements ('S+P = 60' vs 'P=40%, S=60%', which implies S+P=100).
evidence: Panel (a) green 'with prefix cache' curve reads approximately 100, 80, 73, 68, 64, 63 GFLOPs/req at r = 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15. That matches S + P/r with S=60, P=40 (100, 80, 73.3, 68, 64, 62.7). The printed (S+P)/r would give 100, 50, 33.3, 20, 10, 6.7 - not what is drawn. Note line 1 reads 'f(r)=(S+P)/r | S+P = 60' while line 2 reads 'P=40%, S=60%'. Caption: 'the in-plot note's f(r)=(S+P)/r uses P = 40% - the reusable prefix share of the prompt - and S = 60% - the unique suffix'. A reader who copies the printed formula understates cached prefill cost by up to ~6x at r=10 (10 vs 64 GFLOPs/req).
acceptance_test: In the figure source replace the note with 'f(r) = S + P/r; S = 60 GFLOPs, P = 40 GFLOPs, S+P = 100 GFLOPs' and update the caption to the same form. Re-render and confirm the printed curve still matches the printed formula at r = 2, 5, 10 (80, 68, 64 GFLOPs/req).

issue: The caption attributes the caching -> decode-goodput claim to panel (b), but panel (b) plots only decode goodput vs batch size with a single unlabeled curve and no caching dimension; the caching effect the caption claims the panel shows is not visible anywhere in the panel.
evidence: Caption: 'caching raises decode goodput (right: decode goodput vs batch size, arbitrary goodput units, rising with diminishing gains as HBM bandwidth approaches saturation ...)'. Panel (b) contains one blue curve, one red dashed threshold at batch 10, and a red text note; there is no with-cache / no-cache pair and no legend, so the reader cannot see any caching effect. The figure title ('Prefix caching vs batching: two independent effects') is satisfied by (a)=caching, (b)=batching, which makes the caption's parenthetical the only place the caching->goodput claim is tied to (b).
acceptance_test: Either add a second curve to panel (b) distinguishing cached vs uncached decode goodput (with a legend), or rewrite the caption so panel (b) is described only as the batching effect and the caching->goodput claim is stated in prose with its own evidence.

issue: The red annotation block in panel (b) occupies the same plot region as the rising blue curve; at print size the curve runs into the text.
evidence: The five-line red note ('diminishing gains / past ~10 (no hard / plateau; goodput / still rises; tail / latency keeps rising)') sits in the upper-left of panel (b). The blue curve rises from ~50 a.u. at batch 5 to ~80 a.u. at batch 10 through that same band, so the curve enters the text block around the 'still rises; tail' / 'latency keeps rising)' lines.
acceptance_test: Move the note to the lower-right of panel (b) or outside the axes; confirm in the rendered PDF (300 dpi) that no curve stroke intersects any annotation glyph.

issue: In-plot annotation text appears below the 8 pt print floor for figure annotations.
evidence: The green note in panel (a) ('f(r)=(S+P)/r | S+P = 60' / 'P=40%, S=60%') and the red note in panel (b) render visibly smaller than the axis tick labels and axis titles in the same figure; by eye at 150 dpi they are roughly 1-2 pt smaller than the ~9-10 pt axis labels, i.e. below 8 pt.
acceptance_test: Set all in-figure annotation text to >= 8 pt (or move it into the caption) and confirm the rendered glyph height at 300 dpi.

issue: Unit mismatch between caption and axis: the caption describes the left panel as 'as a percent of no-cache prefill work' while the y-axis is labelled 'Prefill FLOPs / req (GFLOPs)'.
evidence: Caption: 'left: prefill work vs average prefix reuse, as a percent of no-cache prefill work, lower is better'. Axis: 'Prefill FLOPs / req (GFLOPs)' with ticks 0-100. The two coincide numerically only because no-cache = 100 GFLOPs, so the reader cannot tell which unit the curve is in.
acceptance_test: State one unit in both places (recommend GFLOPs/req, with 'no-cache = 100 GFLOPs/req' noted in the caption) and confirm the caption no longer says 'percent'.

issue: Both x-axes are linear but carry only two labelled ticks (1 and 10), so the intermediate data points (2, 3, 5) cannot be read off the axis.
evidence: Panel (a) 'Avg prefix reuse' and panel (b) 'Decode batch size' show tick labels '1' and '10' only, with the axis running to ~15-16; the spacing of the '10' label is consistent with a linear scale, so the plotted markers at r = 2, 3, 5 and batch 2, 3, 5 are unlabelled.
acceptance_test: Add ticks at 2, 3, 5 (and 15) on both x-axes, or switch to a log axis with ticks at 1, 2, 5, 10; confirm every plotted marker has a readable x value.

issue: The caption contains a garbled token where a symbol is expected: 'so x = no sharing and hence no prefix reduction'.
evidence: Caption text: 'average prefill reuse = mean number of requests served from each cached prefix block, so x = no sharing and hence no prefix reduction'. The intended statement is presumably 'r = 1 = no sharing' (or 'zero sharing').
acceptance_test: Inspect the source string and replace the stray glyph with the intended symbol; confirm the caption reads as a complete clause.

issue: The prose that describes Fig 16.1 lists three figure features that are not present in the rendered figure, so the reader's map of the figure is wrong before they reach it.
evidence: Printed p. 282: 'The figure marks the canonical-price point (star) and the full sensitivity span (horizontal line), annotates the feasible bound (24.96M = 40 rps x 624,000 active s), and shades the infeasible region beyond it.' In the rendered Fig 16.1 the canonical point is a green diamond (legend: 'cloud $87.6K/mo @ 6.24M (occupancy input)'), not a star; the sensitivity span appears only as the red text 'sensitivity = 6.2-10.4M' inside an annotation box, with no horizontal line; and the feasible bound is labelled 'feasible max 24.96M' with no derivation. Only the hatched infeasible region matches the prose.
acceptance_test: Reconcile prose and figure: either add the star marker, the horizontal sensitivity-span segment and the '24.96M = 40 rps x 624,000 active s' derivation to Fig 16.1, or rewrite the printed p. 282 sentence to name only the features the figure actually contains (green diamond, red price band, dashed managed line, feasible-max label, hatched region).

issue: The managed $20.8/1K line - the line that defines the ~7.5M break-even the caption highlights - is drawn inside the $15-25/1K band in the same hue, so it is not separable, and in grayscale it collapses into the band.
evidence: At the canonical 6.24M req/mo the band spans $93.6K-$156K and the managed line sits at $129.8K, i.e. strictly inside the band; both are rendered in the red/salmon family. In grayscale the band and the dashed managed line fall at nearly the same tone, so the reader cannot locate the crossing with the blue $155.8K/mo self-host line that the caption calls the break-even.
acceptance_test: Render the figure in grayscale and confirm the managed line is separable from the band (distinct dash pattern, heavier weight, or a leader/label at the crossing); alternatively annotate the crossing point directly on the plot.

issue: The vertical dotted line carrying the 'feasible max 24.96M' label appears to be drawn near the canonical 6.24M marker rather than at the feasible bound, so the label may be attached to the wrong line.
evidence: The figure contains exactly one vertical dotted line. 24.96M should sit at ~85% of the log x-axis (log10 2.496e7 = 7.40 within the 4->8 range) and coincide with the left edge of the hatched INFEASIBLE region; 6.24M sits at ~70% (log10 6.24e6 = 6.80). As rendered, the dotted line appears to fall essentially on the green diamond at 6.24M, while the hatched boundary sits further right.
acceptance_test: In the source, assert that the dotted line's x data value equals 2.496e7 and that it coincides with the hatched region's left edge; re-render and confirm the 'feasible max 24.96M' label sits directly above that line and that the canonical 6.24M marker is not conflated with it.

issue: Legend, annotation-box and axis text appear below the 8 pt print floor for figure annotations.
evidence: The red 'break-even ~ 7.5M / sensitivity = 6.2-10.4M / canonical 6.24M req/mo' box, the green 'cloud $87.6K/mo (occupancy input) / priced at 6.24M req/mo only' box, the four-entry legend and the axis titles all render at a small size, visibly below the body text on the same page and below the 8 pt figure-annotation floor.

issue: Fig 16.1 appears seven printed pages after the first substantive discussion of its content, and the reader is asked to reason about 'the shape of the cost functions' and the shaded region (printed pp. 278-279) before seeing the figure.

Printed p. 281 carries only a pointer ('Note 16.1 - (Fig 16.1) - line definitions and the cloud marker'). The figure itself is on printed p. 286.

figure: Figure 17.1 'Sizing a fleet of one model'
issue: Two annotation strings are drawn on top of each other in the upper-left of the plot area, making both partly illegible.
evidence: Around x = 0.3-4.5 h, y ~ 8.5-9.5 req/s the blue label 'N = 4 fleet (3 working + 1 reserve, ~8.0, ideal)' is superimposed with a second string containing '...N-1 reserve so y still clear it after one host drains: N_provisioned = (8.0 - 5.5) / (1.4 - 0.917) = 3 residual hosts (not a measured load curve)'. The superposition produces an unreadable jumble where the N-1 derivation - the figure's only sizing derivation - should be.
acceptance_test: Re-lay the annotations so no two text objects overlap (e.g. move the N-1 derivation into the top-right box or into the caption); confirm in the rendered PDF that no glyph pairs intersect and that the N-1 derivation is fully legible.

issue: The caption contains a verbatim splice of the figure's internal annotation, producing an ungrammatical caption and duplicating in-figure text.
evidence: Caption: '...so a 3-host fleet (3x0.9 req/s) is sized above it; 3 hosts clear the 5.5 req/s burst at p = 1.4h is the N-1 reserve so y still clear it after one host drains: N_provisioned = (8.0 - 5.5) / (1.4 - 0.917) = 3 residual hosts (not a measured load curve). Burst profile: ...'. The clause from 'at p = 1.4h' through '(not a measured load curve)' is the figure's internal annotation pasted into the caption mid-sentence; the caption then separately states 'Burst profile: the burst curve is an illustrative Gaussian-shaped profile, not a measured load curve', duplicating the same disclaimer.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption as continuous prose that states the conclusion (3 hosts x 2.0 req/s = 6.0 req/s at p = 1 clears the 5.5 req/s burst; break-even p = 0.917) and delete the spliced fragment; confirm no caption sentence duplicates an in-figure annotation verbatim.

issue: The printed derivation does not evaluate to its stated result and is dimensionally incoherent: 'N_provisioned = (8.0 - 5.5) / (1.4 - 0.917) = 3 residual hosts'.
evidence: 2.5 / 0.483 = 5.18, not 3. The denominator also mixes a duration (1.4 h) with a dimensionless factor (0.917), so the expression has no consistent unit. The figure's own break-even p = 0.917 is exactly 5.5 / (3 x 2.0) = 0.9167, and the caption's 'at p = 0.85 it is 3 x 0.85 = 2.55 req/s' uses the same missing per-host factor, so the intended derivation is almost certainly N = 5.5 / (2.0 p) = 3 at p = 0.917 (equivalently p_break-even = 5.5 / 6.0). A reader who copies the printed expression over-provisions by ~73%.
acceptance_test: Replace the printed expression with 'p_break-even = 5.5 / (3 x 2.0) = 0.917' (or 'N = 5.5 / (2.0 p) = 3 at p = 0.917'); confirm the printed expression evaluates to the printed result and that all quantities in it share a unit.
